title: Every create rewrites the guest init and initramfs source in place, so a create beside it can hash an empty file
foundBy: session agent, from a smoke-tier replay on a cold private cache whose create failed with a missing modules.tar, 2026-11-14
details:
`GuestInitPath` and `GuestInitramfsSrcPath` (assets.go) write the embedded `image/guest/init` and `image/guest/initramfs-init.c` into the cache as `guest-init` and `guest-initramfs-init.c` on every create, with `os.WriteFile`. That call truncates the file and then writes it. Other creates read the same two files at the same time and hash them. The init's hash is a field of the base-rootfs stamp (`internal/fcdisk/build.go`, `inithash`). The source's hash is in the kernel set's key (`kernelSetKey` through `initramfsStamp`). A reader in the gap hashes an empty file.

Two failures follow, each reproduced on a private cache with eight creates at once, each in its own group.

1. Kernel set. The key comes out as `<NVR.arch>-fedora-39ab9907` instead of `-9de5f54f` for kernel pin `koji:7.2.5-200.fc44`. That is sha256 of the pin, a bar, and `v1-static-init-` plus the first 12 hex digits of sha256 of nothing. On a cold cache the base-rootfs build then fails with `tar: <cache>/kernels/7.2.5-200.fc44.x86_64-fedora-39ab9907/modules.tar: Cannot open: No such file or directory`. On a warm cache the create starts a kernel build under the stray key. That build compiles the source it reads, which can be the empty file again: `undefined reference to 'main'`. An empty `kernels/<NVR.arch>-fedora-39ab9907/` folder is left behind.

2. Base rootfs. The stamp's init field comes out as `e3b0c44298fc`, the hash of an empty file. The stamp no longer matches, so the create rebuilds the image's slot in place with an empty `/fc-init`. `debugfs -R "stat /fc-init"` on the slot reports `Size: 0`. Every later create from that slot fails with `microVM "<name>" exited before becoming ready`, until a create reads the whole file and rebuilds the slot again.

The gap is short. 24 creates in three rounds of eight on a warm cache all passed, and only the first cold-cache create hit it unaided. A helper widened it by truncating and rewriting the same bytes in a loop. Under it, one round of eight lost 5 creates to the kernel key, and the next lost all 8 to the empty init. Every host that runs creates in parallel on one cache is exposed, since the slot and the kernel set are shared there. The base-rootfs half is older than the keyed kernel sets: the same write and the same stamp field are in a0df4c5.

A workaround already in the binary: with `CS_SANDBOX_ASSETS_DIR` naming a clean checkout at the binary's own commit, both paths resolve to the checkout's files, and nothing is written. Three rounds of eight passed 24 of 24, 16 of them with both files under the rewriting helper. No stray kernel set appeared, and the one rebuild was the first round repairing the slot left empty above. `cs-sandbox agent-tools` and `cs-sandbox version` printed the same bytes with and without it. The fix is to write these files only when their bytes differ, through a temporary file renamed over the old one.

Not covered here: the stamps themselves are written in place too (`writeStamp`, `KernelSet.writeStamp`), by a build, while a create beside it may read them.
